---
title: "Commands"
---

Six commands. Each is resumable, and each caches what it fetches, so re-running does only
what is missing.

## `oai-pmh`

Reads a collection's OAI-PMH records into `thesis`, `thesis_metadata`, and the keyword
tables.

```bash
skemman oai-pmh
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--location`, `-l` | Collection handle, e.g. `1946/2064`; mapped to `com_1946_2064`. Default: every handle in config. |
| `--set` | Exact OAI-PMH setSpec to harvest. Default: every handle in config. |
| `--year-start` | First `dc:date` year to keep. Default: `year_start` in config. |
| `--year-end` | Last `dc:date` year to keep. Default: `year_end` in config. |
| `--limit` | Stop after N records per set. Default: `record_limit` in config; blank means all. |
| `--metadata-prefix` | OAI-PMH metadata prefix. Default `oai_dc`. |
| `--cache-dir` | Cache directory for OAI-PMH XML pages. Default `data/raw/oai`. |
| `--output`, `-o` | Database path. |

Re-running the configured handles picks up newly deposited theses; existing ids are left
alone.

Use `--metadata-prefix xoai` to cache DSpace's richer OAI format for attached files:

```bash
skemman oai-pmh --metadata-prefix xoai
```

## `metadata-load`

Reloads normalized metadata from cached OAI-PMH XML.

```bash
skemman metadata-load --ids 25337
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--ids` | Comma-separated thesis ids. Default: every id already in `thesis`. |
| `--oai-dir` | OAI XML cache directory. Default `data/raw/oai`. |

## `files-load`

Loads file rows from cached `xoai` pages. **No network.**

```bash
skemman files-load
```

This fills `thesis_file` with filename, byte size, file type, download URL and a
`primary`/`secondary` role inferred from DSpace's bundle description and the filename.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--ids` | Comma-separated thesis ids. Default: every id found in cached `xoai`. |
| `--oai-dir` | OAI XML cache directory. Default `data/raw/oai`. |

## `files-index`

Fetches item pages and stores only their file tables in `thesis_file`.

```bash
skemman files-index
```

This adds Skemman's explicit open/closed labels to the file rows.

For most runs, `files-load` is enough. Use `files-index` when Skemman's explicit open/closed
labels are needed before trying PDF downloads.

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--ids` | Comma-separated thesis ids. Default: everything not yet indexed. |
| `--limit` | Stop after N theses. |
| `--config`, `-c` | Config path for base URL, user-agent, delay and timeout. |

## `titlepage-load`

Fetches open PDFs and reads their title pages into `thesis_titlepage`.

```bash
skemman titlepage-load --degree-level master --max-mb 50
```

| Option | Meaning |
| --- | --- |
| `--degree-level` | `master` (default), `bachelor`, `phd`. |
| `--limit` | Stop after N theses. |
| `--ids` | Specific ids, ignoring the failure filter. |
| `--pages` | PDF pages to keep as text. Default: `titlepage_pages` in config; blank means the whole PDF. |
| `--max-mb` | Skip PDFs larger than this. |
| `--include-closed` | Try files the item page marks closed. |
| `--retry-failed` | Retry ones recorded as permanently unavailable. |
| `--keep-pdf` | Keep the downloaded PDFs. |
| `--log` | Failure log path. Default `logs/titlepage.log`. |

## `clean-people`

Normalizes names already loaded: strips embedded birth years and parenthesized roles.

```bash
skemman clean-people
```
